title: Conditions on Which a Sponsoring Group Holds an Employer and Union Group Retiree Plan
content:
A retiree may be held on a plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans only where all of the following stand together, on every plan of the book alike:

1. The retiree is entitled to Medicare Part A.
2. The retiree is enrolled in Medicare Part B.
3. The retiree is named on the sponsor's eligibility file.
4. The sponsor's group contract is in force.
5. The sponsoring group enrols at least the smallest number of retirees scheduled for that plan.

A Medicare-eligible spouse or dependent may be enrolled on every plan of the book.

| Group plan | Smallest number of retirees the sponsor must enrol | Medicare-eligible spouse or dependent may be enrolled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Standard (PPO) | 100 | Yes |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Enhanced (PPO) | 250 | Yes |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) | 500 | Yes |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Standard (EGWP) | 100 | Yes |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Enhanced (EGWP) | 250 | Yes |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP) | 500 | Yes |

## Points of judgement on the conditions

The group size figure is the smallest number the sponsor must enrol to hold that plan, so a sponsor enrolling exactly 250 retirees satisfies the condition on Ridgecrest Group Retiree Enhanced (PPO), and a sponsor enrolling 249 does not.

The first four conditions are the same on every plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans; only the group size figure moves, standing at 100, 250 and 500 across the book.

The first two conditions are about the retiree's own standing with Medicare, the third and fourth about the sponsor's file and its contract. All four must stand, so a retiree entitled to Part A and enrolled in Part B is still not held where the sponsor's contract is not in force.
